Since \(AB\) is a diameter, the angles around \(O\) on the upper side form a straight angle of \(180^\circ\). Let \(\theta\) be the central angle of the shaded sector. Then
\[
40^\circ+\theta+35^\circ+30^\circ+20^\circ=180^\circ.
\]
Thus
\[
\theta=180^\circ-125^\circ=55^\circ.
\]
For a uniform point in the disk, the probability of lying in a sector is the ratio of its central angle to \(360^\circ\):
\[
\frac{55}{360}=\frac{11}{72}.
\]
\[
\boxed{\frac{11}{72}}
\]
